wikipedia.extract: Nyctipolus is a genus of South American nightjars in the family Caprimulgidae.
wikipedia.title: Nyctipolus

wikipedia.extract: Ceuthmochares is a genus of 2 species of cuckoos in the family Cuculidae. The two species were once treated as a single species, known as the yellowbill.
wikipedia.title: Ceuthmochares

wikipedia.extract: Plioperdix is an extinct genus of phasianid that lived during the Neogene period.
wikipedia.title: Plioperdix

wikipedia.extract: Palaeoephippiorhynchus is an extinct genus of large stork from the Oligocene of Africa: its closest living relative is the saddle-billed stork.
wikipedia.title: Palaeoephippiorhynchus

wikipedia.extract: Archaeopsittacus is a genus of prehistoric parrot. It is known from deposits of either Late Oligocene or Early Miocene age (c.
wikipedia.title: Archaeopsittacus

wikipedia.extract: Dynamopterus velox is an extinct prehistoric bird, known from a single large right humerus recovered in France. The humerus shares anatomical features with living cuckoos (though it is much larger).
wikipedia.title: Dynamopterus

wikipedia.extract: Eocuculus cherpinae is a prehistoric bird, known from postcranial remains from the late Eocene Florissant beds in Colorado.
wikipedia.title: Eocuculus

commonNames.name: Northern Needle-clawed Galago
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The northern needle-clawed bushbaby (Euoticus pallidus) is a species of strepsirrhine primate in the family Galagidae. It is found in the coastal region of Cameroon and Nigeria, and on the island of Bioko, Equatorial Guinea in lower-elevation forests that provide its specialized diet of tree gum and resins.
wikipedia.title: Northern needle-clawed bushbaby

commonNames.name: Betsileo Woolly Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Avahi betsileo Andriantompohavana, Lei, Zaonarivelo, Engberg, Nalanirina, McGuire, Shore et al., 2007

wikipedia.extract: The Betsileo woolly lemur or Betsileo avahi (Avahi betsileo) is a species of woolly lemur native to southeastern Madagascar, in the District of Fandriana. The pelage differs significantly from other southeastern woolly lemurs in that it is primarily light reddish brown on most of the body and grey under the jaw and on the extremities.
wikipedia.title: Betsileo woolly lemur

commonNames.name: Betsileo Sportive Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Lepilemur betsileo Louis Jr., Engberg, Lei, Geng, Sommer, Randriamampionona, Randriamanana, Zaonarivelo et al., 2006

wikipedia.extract: The Betsileo sportive lemur (Lepilemur betsileo) is a sportive lemur endemic to Madagascar. Like all members of its genus, it is nocturnal and largely folivorous.
wikipedia.title: Betsileo sportive lemur

commonNames.name: Petter's Sportive Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Lepilemur petteri Louis Jr., Engberg, Lei, Geng, Sommer, Randriamampionona, Randriamanana, Zaonarivelo et al., 2006

wikipedia.extract: Petter's sportive lemur (Lepilemur petteri) is a sportive lemur endemic to Madagascar. It is one of 26 species in the genus Lepilemur.
wikipedia.title: Petter's sportive lemur

commonNames.name: Madame Fleurette’s Sportive Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Lepilemur fleuretae Louis Jr., Engberg, Lei, Geng, Sommer, Randriamampionona, Randriamanana, Zaonarivelo et al., 2006

wikipedia.extract: Fleurette's sportive lemur (Lepilemur fleuretae), or the Andohahela sportive lemur, is a sportive lemur endemic to Madagascar. Like all members of its genus, it is nocturnal, and largely folivorous.
wikipedia.title: Fleurette's sportive lemur

gbif.scientificName: Lepilemur ahmansonorum Louis Jr., Engberg, Lei, Geng, Sommer, Randriamampionona, Randriamanana, Zaonarivelo et al., 2006

wikipedia.extract: Ahmanson's sportive lemur (Lepilemur ahmansonorum), or the Tsiombikibo sportive lemur, is a sportive lemur endemic to Madagascar. It is a relatively small sportive lemur with a total length of about 47 to 54 cm (19 to 21 in), of which 23–25 cm (9.1–9.8 in) are tail.
wikipedia.title: Ahmanson's sportive lemur

commonNames.name: Nosy Be Sportive Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

commonNames.name: Hawks' Sportive Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Lepilemur tymerlachsoni Louis Jr., Engberg, Lei, Geng, Sommer, Randriamampionona, Randriamanana, Zaonarivelo et al., 2006

wikipedia.extract: Hawks' sportive lemur (Lepilemur tymerlachsoni), also known as the Nosy Be sportive lemur or Nosy Be weasel lemur, is a sportive lemur endemic to Madagascar. Like all members of its genus, it is solitary, nocturnal and largely folivorous.
wikipedia.title: Hawks' sportive lemur

commonNames.name: Daraina Sportive Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Lepilemur milanoii Louis Jr., Engberg, Lei, Geng, Sommer, Randriamampionona, Randriamanana, Zaonarivelo et al., 2006

wikipedia.extract: The Daraina sportive lemur (Lepilemur milanoii) is a sportive lemur endemic to Madagascar. It is a relatively small sportive lemur with a total length of about 49 to 56 cm (19 to 22 in), of which 24–27 cm (9.4–10.6 in) are tail.
wikipedia.title: Daraina sportive lemur

commonNames.name: Sambirano Fork-marked Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Pariente's fork-marked lemur (Phaner parienti), or the Sambirano fork-marked lemur, is a species of lemur endemic to the Sambirano region of north-western Madagascar. This lemur has light brown to gray upperparts, a prominent facial fork and dorsal stripe that runs from the tail's tip to the point where it splits on the lemur's head to rejoin at the nose, and a white-tipped tail.
wikipedia.title: Pariente's fork-marked lemur

wikipedia.extract: The Amber Mountain fork-marked lemur (Phaner electromontis), also known as the Montagne d'Ambre fork-crowned lemur or Tanta, is a small primate, and like the other lemurs, can only be found on the island of Madagascar. The species is named after the Amber Mountain National Park where they are found.
wikipedia.title: Amber Mountain fork-marked lemur

commonNames.name: Alaotra Reed Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Lac Alaotra bamboo lemur (Hapalemur alaotrensis), also known as the Lac Alaotra gentle lemur, Alaotran bamboo lemur, Alaotran gentle lemur, Alaotra reed lemur, or locally as the bandro, is a bamboo lemur. It is endemic to the reed beds in and around Lac Alaotra, in northeast Madagascar.
wikipedia.title: Lac Alaotra bamboo lemur

commonNames.name: Juruá Red Howler Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

commonNames.name: Juruá Red Howler
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

commonNames.name: Juruá Red Howling Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Juruá red howler (Alouatta juara) is a species of howler monkey, native to Peru and Brazil.
wikipedia.title: Juruá red howler

commonNames.name: Maranhão Red-handed Howler Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Maranhão red-handed howler (Alouatta ululata) is an endangered species of howler monkey endemic to forests (for example Babaçu forests) in the northeastern Brazilian states of Ceará, Maranhão and Piauí. It was previously thought to be a subspecies of the red-handed howler, but unlike that species, the Maranhão red-handed howler is strongly sexually dichromatic.
wikipedia.title: Maranhão red-handed howler

commonNames.name: Black Squirrel Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The black squirrel monkey (Saimiri vanzolinii), also known as the blackish squirrel monkey or black-headed squirrel monkey, is a small New World primate, endemic to the central Amazon in Brazil. It largely resembles the female of the far more common Bolivian squirrel monkey, though the latter lacks the black central back.
wikipedia.title: Black squirrel monkey

wikipedia.extract: The gold-and-white marmoset (Mico chrysoleucos), also known as the golden-white tassel-ear marmoset, is a species of marmoset, a small monkey endemic to the Amazon rainforest in eastern Amazonas state, Brazil.
wikipedia.title: Gold-and-white marmoset

commonNames.name: Buffy-headed Marmoset
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The buffy-headed marmoset (Callithrix flaviceps) is a rare species of marmoset endemic to the rainforests of south-eastern Brazil. It occurs in southern Espírito Santo and possibly northern Rio de Janeiro and its distribution extends into Minas Gerais.
wikipedia.title: Buffy-headed marmoset

commonNames.name: Aripuanã Marmoset
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Hershkovitz's marmoset (Mico intermedius), also known as the Aripuanã marmoset is a marmoset species endemic to the south-central Amazon rainforest in Brazil. The common name is a reference to American zoologist Philip Hershkovitz.
wikipedia.title: Hershkovitz's marmoset

commonNames.name: Marca’s Marmoset
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Marca's marmoset (Mico marcai) is a species of marmoset that is endemic to the Amazon, in the Aripuanã-Manicoré interfluvium in Brazil. Its body is light grey, with orange legs, a black tail, a pinkish face, and naked ears.
wikipedia.title: Marca's marmoset

commonNames.name: Black-headed Marmoset
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The black-headed marmoset (Mico nigriceps) is a marmoset species endemic to Brazil. It inhabits humid tropical rainforest, mostly second growth and edge; the distribution is not exactly known but is thought to be Rio dos Marmelos in the north and east, Madeira River in the west and Ji-Paraná River in the south.
wikipedia.title: Black-headed marmoset

commonNames.name: Equatorial Saki
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The equatorial saki (Pithecia aequatorialis), also called the red-bearded saki, is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey. It is found in northeastern Peru and Ecuador.
wikipedia.title: Equatorial saki

wikipedia.extract: The ornate titi monkey (Plecturocebus ornatus) is a species of titi monkey and is the smallest member of the family Pitheciidae, which also includes uakaris and saki monkeys. As it is a member of this family, it is classified as a type of New World monkey.
wikipedia.title: Ornate titi monkey

commonNames.name: Madidi Titi Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Madidi titi monkey, also known as the GoldenPalace.com monkey or the golden palace monkey, is a titi, a kind of New World monkey, discovered in western Bolivia's Madidi National Park in 2004. Its scientific name is Plecturocebus aureipalatii, the specific epithet meaning "of the Golden Palace", in reference to GoldenPalace.com, an online casino.
wikipedia.title: Madidi titi monkey

commonNames.name: Olalla Brothers’ Titi
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Olalla brothers's titi monkey (Plecturocebus olallae) is a species of titi monkey, a type of New World monkey, endemic to Bolivia. There are between 110 and 150 individuals in the wild.
wikipedia.title: Olalla brothers' titi monkey

commonNames.name: Black-handed Titi
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The coastal black-handed titi monkey (Callicebus melanochir) is a species of titi, a type of New World monkey, endemic to Brazil.
wikipedia.title: Coastal black-handed titi monkey

commonNames.name: Ashy Black Titi Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The ashy black titi monkey (Plecturocebus cinerascens) is a species of titi monkey, a type of New World monkey, endemic to Brazil. It was originally described as Callicebus cinerascens in 1823 and was changed to genus Plecturocebus in 2016.
wikipedia.title: Ashy black titi monkey

commonNames.name: Yellow-handed Titi Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Lucifer titi monkey (Cheracebus lucifer) is a species of titi, a type of New World monkey, from South America. It is found in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.
wikipedia.title: Lucifer titi monkey

wikipedia.extract: Hershkovitz's titi monkey (Plecturocebus dubius) is a species of titi monkey, a type of New World monkey, from South America. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.
wikipedia.title: Hershkovitz's titi monkey

commonNames.name: Colombian Black-handed Titi
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Colombian black-handed titi monkey (Cheracebus medemi) is a species of titi, a type of New World monkey, endemic to Colombia. It was originally described in the genus Callicebus in 1963.
wikipedia.title: Colombian black-handed titi monkey

commonNames.name: Baptista Lake Titi Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Baptista Lake titi monkey (Plecturocebus baptista) is a species of titi monkey, a type of New World monkey, endemic to Brazil. It was originally described as Callicebus baptista in 1939.
wikipedia.title: Baptista Lake titi monkey

commonNames.name: Blond Titi Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Barbara Brown's titi monkey (Callicebus barbarabrownae), also popularly known as the blond titi monkey or northern Bahian blond titi, is a species of titi, a type of New World monkey. This critically endangered species is endemic to the Caatinga in northeastern Brazil, and it is estimated that less than 250 mature individuals remain.
wikipedia.title: Barbara Brown's titi monkey

wikipedia.extract: The collared titi monkey (Cheracebus torquatus) is a species of titi, a type of New World monkey. It is endemic to northern Brazil.
wikipedia.title: Collared titi monkey

commonNames.name: Hernández-Camacho’s Night Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Hernández-Camacho's night monkey (Aotus jorgehernandezi) is a species of night monkey of the family Aotidae. It was first described in 2007 by Thomas Defler and Marta Bueno.
wikipedia.title: Hernández-Camacho's night monkey

commonNames.name: Lowe's Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Lowe's mona monkey (Cercopithecus lowei) is an Old World monkey in the family Cercopithecidae found from the Ivory Coast to Ghana. It was previously classified as a subspecies of Campbell's mona monkey C. campbelli.
wikipedia.title: Lowe's mona monkey

wikipedia.extract: The golden monkey (Cercopithecus mitis kandti) is a subspecies of the blue monkey. It is an Old World monkey found in the Virunga volcanic mountains of Central Africa, including four national parks: Mgahinga, in south-west Uganda; Volcanoes, in north-west Rwanda; and Virunga and Kahuzi-Biéga, in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
wikipedia.title: Golden monkey

wikipedia.extract: The silver monkey (Cercopithecus mitis doggetti) is a subspecies of the blue monkey (Cercopithecus mitis). It is an Old World monkey found primarily in East Africa.
wikipedia.title: Silver monkey

wikipedia.extract: The Dryas monkey (Chlorocebus dryas), also known as Salonga monkey, ekele, or inoko, is a little-known species of Old World monkey found only in the Congo Basin, restricted to the left bank of the Congo River. It is now established that the animals that had been classified as Cercopithecus salongo (the common name being Zaire Diana monkey) were in fact Dryas monkeys.
wikipedia.title: Dryas monkey

commonNames.name: Kashmir Gray Langur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Kashmir gray langur (Semnopithecus ajax) is an Old World monkey, one of the langur species. It is a leaf-eating monkey.
wikipedia.title: Kashmir gray langur

commonNames.name: Black-footed Gray Langur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The black-footed gray langur (Semnopithecus hypoleucos) is an Old World monkey, one of the species of langurs. Found in southern India, this, like other gray langurs, is a leaf-eating monkey.
wikipedia.title: Black-footed gray langur

commonNames.name: Nepal Gray Langur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Nepal gray langur (Semnopithecus schistaceus) is a gray langur endemic to the Himalayas in Nepal, far southwestern Tibet, northern India, northern Pakistan, Bhutan and possibly Afghanistan. It is found in forests at an elevation of 1,500 to 4,000 metres (4,900 to 13,100 ft).
wikipedia.title: Nepal gray langur

wikipedia.extract: The Indochinese black langur (Trachypithecus ebenus) is a poorly known Old World monkey native to Laos and adjacent Vietnam. It was originally described as a subspecies of T. auratus, but was later found to be a member of the T. francoisi group, with some maintaining it as a subspecies of that species.
wikipedia.title: Indochinese black langur

wikipedia.extract: Dolichopithecus is an extinct genus of Old World monkey that lived in Europe during the Late Miocene and Pliocene.
wikipedia.title: Dolichopithecus

wikipedia.extract: Mesopithecus ("middle monkey" for being between Hylobates and Semnopithecus in build) is an extinct genus of Old World monkey belonging to the subfamily Colobinae that lived in Eurasia during the Late Miocene and Pliocene epochs, around 8.2-2.6 million years ago.
wikipedia.title: Mesopithecus

wikipedia.extract: Homo erectus ( lit. 'upright man') is an extinct species of archaic human from the Pleistocene, spanning nearly 2 million years. It is the first human species to evolve a humanlike body plan and gait, to leave Africa and colonize Asia and Europe, and to wield fire.
wikipedia.title: Homo erectus

wikipedia.extract: Homo rudolfensis is an extinct species of archaic human from the Early Pleistocene of East Africa about 2 million years ago (mya). Because H. rudolfensis coexisted with several other hominins, it is debated what specimens can be confidently assigned to this species beyond the lectotype skull KNM-ER 1470 and other partial skull aspects.
wikipedia.title: Homo rudolfensis

wikipedia.extract: Homo heidelbergensis () is a controversial and somewhat poorly defined species of archaic human from the Middle Pleistocene of Europe and Africa, as well as potentially Asia depending on the taxonomic convention used. The species-level classification of Homo during the Middle Pleistocene is controversial, called the "muddle in the middle", owing to the wide anatomical range of variation that populations exhibited during this time.
wikipedia.title: Homo heidelbergensis

wikipedia.extract: Homo habilis (lit. 'handy man') is an extinct species of archaic human from the Early Pleistocene of East and South Africa about 2.4 million years ago to 1.65 million years ago (mya).
wikipedia.title: Homo habilis

gbif.scientificName: Homo antecessor Bermúdez de Castro et al., 1997

wikipedia.extract: Homo antecessor (Latin for 'pioneer man') is an extinct species of archaic human recorded in the Spanish Sierra de Atapuerca, a productive archaeological site, from 1.2 to 0.8 million years ago during the Early Pleistocene. Populations of this species may have been present elsewhere in Western Europe, and were among the first to settle that region of the world, hence the name.
wikipedia.title: Homo antecessor

wikipedia.extract: Lufengpithecus (from Lufeng County, and Ancient Greek πίθηκος (píthēkos), meaning "ape, monkey") is an extinct genus of ape, known from the Late Miocene of East Asia. It is known from thousands of dental remains and a few skulls and probably weighed about 50 kg (110 lb).
wikipedia.title: Lufengpithecus

gbif.scientificName: Sahelanthropus Brunet, Guy, Pilbeam, Mackaye et al., 2002

wikipedia.extract: Sahelanthropus is an extinct genus of hominid dated to about 7 million years ago during the Late Miocene. The type species, Sahelanthropus tchadensis, was first announced in 2002, based mainly on a partial cranium, nicknamed Toumaï, discovered in northern Chad.
wikipedia.title: Sahelanthropus

wikipedia.extract: Paranthropus boisei is a species of australopithecine from the Early Pleistocene of East Africa about 2.5 to 1.15 million years ago. The holotype specimen, OH 5, was discovered by palaeoanthropologist Mary Leakey in 1959 at Olduvai Gorge, Tanzania and described by her husband Louis a month later.
wikipedia.title: Paranthropus boisei

wikipedia.extract: Paranthropus is a genus of extinct hominin which contains three widely accepted species: P. aethiopicus, P. robustus and P. boisei. However, the validity of Paranthropus is contested, and it is sometimes considered to be synonymous with Australopithecus.
wikipedia.title: Paranthropus

gbif.scientificName: Pierolapithecus Moyà-Solà, Köhler, Alba, Casanovas-Vilar & Galindo, 2004

wikipedia.extract: Pierolapithecus catalaunicus is an extinct species of ape that lived during the Middle Miocene, about 13–12.5 million years ago, in Catalonia, Spain. Described in 2004 from a partial skeleton discovered near Els Hostalets de Pierola, it is represented by one of the most complete Miocene ape skeletons from Europe.
wikipedia.title: Pierolapithecus

wikipedia.extract: Gigantopithecus ( jy-gan-toh-pih-THEE-kəs, -⁠PITH-ih-kəs, jih-) is an extinct genus of great ape that lived in central to southern China from two million to approximately 215,000–295,000 years ago during the Early to Middle Pleistocene, represented by one species, Gigantopithecus blacki. The first remains of Gigantopithecus, two third-molar teeth, were identified in a drugstore by anthropologist Ralph von Koenigswald in 1935 in England, who subsequently described the ape.
wikipedia.title: Gigantopithecus

wikipedia.extract: Micropithecus is an extinct genus of primates that lived in East Africa about 19 to 15 million years ago, during the early Miocene. The genus and its type species, Micropithecus clarki, were first scientifically described in 1978.
wikipedia.title: Micropithecus

wikipedia.extract: Kenyapithecus wickeri is a fossil ape discovered by Louis Leakey in 1961 at a site called Fort Ternan in Kenya. The upper jaw and teeth were dated to 14 million years ago.
wikipedia.title: Kenyapithecus

wikipedia.extract: Ardipithecus is a genus of extinct hominine that lived during the Late Miocene and Early Pliocene epochs in the Afar Depression, Ethiopia. Originally described as one of the earliest ancestors of humans after they diverged from the last common ancestor shared with chimpanzees, the relation of this genus to human ancestors and whether it is a hominin is now a matter of debate.
wikipedia.title: Ardipithecus

wikipedia.extract: Paranthropus robustus is an extinct species of robust australopithecine from the Early and possibly Middle Pleistocene of the Cradle of Humankind, South Africa, about 2.27 to 0.87 (or, more conservatively, 2 to 1) million years ago. It has been identified in Kromdraai, Swartkrans, Sterkfontein, Gondolin, Cooper's, and Drimolen Caves.
wikipedia.title: Paranthropus robustus

gbif.scientificName: Morotopithecus Gebo, MacLatchy, Kityo, Deino, Kingston & Pilbeam, 1997

wikipedia.extract: Morotopithecus is a genus of fossil ape discovered in Miocene-age deposits of Moroto, Uganda. The phylogenetic status of Morotopithecus bishopi is debated to the extent that it challenges established views on the connection between Miocene primates and extant hominids (i.e.
wikipedia.title: Morotopithecus

wikipedia.extract: Paranthropus aethiopicus is an extinct species of robust australopithecine from the Late Pliocene to Early Pleistocene of East Africa about 2.7–2.3 million years ago. However, it is much debated whether or not Paranthropus is an invalid grouping and is synonymous with Australopithecus, so the species is also often classified as Australopithecus aethiopicus.
wikipedia.title: Paranthropus aethiopicus

wikipedia.extract: Dryopithecus is a genus of extinct great apes from the middle–late Miocene boundary of Europe 12.5 to 11.1 million years ago (mya). Since its discovery in 1856, the genus has been subject to taxonomic turmoil, with numerous new species being described from single remains based on minute differences amongst each other, and the fragmentary nature of the holotype specimen makes differentiating remains difficult.
wikipedia.title: Dryopithecus

wikipedia.extract: Graecopithecus is an extinct genus of hominid that lived in southeast Europe during the late Miocene around 7.2 million years ago. Originally identified by a single lower jawbone bearing teeth found in Pyrgos Vasilissis, Athens, Greece, in 1944, other teeth potentially belonging to this taxon were discovered from Azmaka quarry in Bulgaria in 2012.
wikipedia.title: Graecopithecus

wikipedia.extract: Catopithecus is an early catarrhine fossil. It is known from more than 16 specimens of a single species, Catopithecus browni, found in the Jebel Qatrani Formation of the Faiyum Governorate, Egypt.
wikipedia.title: Catopithecus

wikipedia.extract: Proconsulidae is an early family of primates that lived during the Miocene epoch in Kenya, and was restricted to Africa. Members of the family have a mixture of Old World monkey and ape characteristics, so the placement in the ape superfamily Hominoidea is tentative; some scientists place Proconsulidae outside of Hominoidea in a separate superfamily Proconsuloidea, before the split of the apes and Old World monkeys.
wikipedia.title: Proconsulidae

wikipedia.extract: Proconsul africanus was an ape which lived from about 23 to 14 million years ago during the Miocene epoch. It was a fruit eater and its brain was larger than that of a monkey, although probably not as large as that of a modern ape.
wikipedia.title: Proconsul africanus

commonNames.name: Anosy Mouse Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Microcebus tanosi Rasoloarison, Weisrock, Yoder, Rakotondravony & Kappeler, 2013

wikipedia.extract: The Anosy mouse lemur (Microcebus tanosi) is a species of mouse lemur known only from the Manantantely Forest and Ivorona Forest in southeastern Madagascar, near Tôlanaro. Specimens were first collected in April 2007, and its discovery was announced in 2013 along with the Marohita mouse lemur (Microcebus marohita).
wikipedia.title: Anosy mouse lemur

commonNames.name: Marohita Mouse Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Microcebus marohita Rasoloarison, Weisrock, Yoder, Rakotondravony & Kappeler, 2013

wikipedia.extract: The Marohita mouse lemur (Microcebus marohita) is a species of mouse lemur known only from the Marohita Forest in eastern Madagascar, near the village of Marolambo. Specimens were first collected in December 2003, and its discovery was announced in 2013 along with the Anosy mouse lemur (Microcebus tanosi).
wikipedia.title: Marohita mouse lemur

wikipedia.extract: Griphopithecus is a prehistoric ape from the Miocene of Turkey and Central Europe.
wikipedia.title: Griphopithecus

wikipedia.extract: Querandiornis romani was a species of Tinamid bird that lived during the Pleistocene.
wikipedia.title: Querandiornis

wikipedia.extract: The banded bay cuckoo or bay-banded cuckoo (Cacomantis sonneratii) is a species of small cuckoo found in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. Like others in the genus they have round nostrils.
wikipedia.title: Banded bay cuckoo

wikipedia.extract: Anabernicula is an extinct genus of waterfowl related to shelducks that existed from the Pliocene to the Pleistocene in North America. Four species have been described: A. minuscula, A. gracilenta, A. oregonensis, and A. robusta.
wikipedia.title: Anabernicula

wikipedia.extract: Telmabates is an extinct genus of presbyornithid bird from the Eocene Bird Clay Locality of the Sarmiento Formation of Chubut Province, Argentina. The genus contains a single species, T. antiquus.
wikipedia.title: Telmabates

wikipedia.extract: Mancalla is an extinct genus of prehistoric flightless alcids that lived on the Pacific coast of today's California and Mexico during the Late Miocene to Early Pliocene.
wikipedia.title: Mancalla

wikipedia.extract: Lyncornis is a genus of nightjars in the nightjar family Caprimulgidae that are found is South and Southeast Asia. The English name "eared nightjar" refers to the two tufts of feathers on their head.
wikipedia.title: Lyncornis

wikipedia.extract: The band-winged nightjar or greater band-winged nightjar (Systellura longirostris) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is the only species now placed in the genus Systellura.
wikipedia.title: Band-winged nightjar

wikipedia.extract: Antrostomus is a genus of nightjars formerly included in the genus Caprimulgus. They are medium-sized nocturnal birds with long pointed wings, short legs and short bills.
wikipedia.title: Antrostomus

wikipedia.extract: Turturoena, commonly called bronze-naped pigeon, is a pigeon subgenus comprising three species: the eastern bronze-naped pigeon, the western bronze-naped pigeon, and the São Tomé bronze-naped pigeon.
wikipedia.title: Turturoena

wikipedia.extract: Delphinornis is an extinct genus of penguins that lived around the middle Eocene to the middle Miocene in Antarctica.
wikipedia.title: Delphinornis

wikipedia.extract: Anthropornis is a genus of giant penguin that lived 45-33 million years ago, during the Late Eocene and the earliest part of the Oligocene.
wikipedia.title: Anthropornis

wikipedia.extract: Arthrodytes is an extinct genus of penguins which contains a single species, whose remains have been recovered from the San Julian Formation (Late Eocene to Early Oligocene) of Patagonia. Other authors report a younger age for the fossils recovered from the Early Miocene Gaiman and Monte León Formations.
wikipedia.title: Arthrodytes

wikipedia.extract: Gallirallus is a genus of rails that live in the Australasian-Pacific region. The genus is characterised by an ability to colonise relatively small and isolated islands and thereafter to evolve flightless forms, many of which became extinct following Polynesian settlement.
wikipedia.title: Gallirallus

wikipedia.extract: Protopelicanus cuvierii is a putative fossil waterbird of uncertain affinities. It was briefly described and figured by Georges Cuvier in 1822 from Late Eocene material from Montmartre, France, though not formally described and named until 1852 by German botanist and ornithologist Ludwig Reichenbach as an early pelecanid.
wikipedia.title: Protopelicanus

wikipedia.extract: Heliadornis is a genus of prehistoric seabirds related to modern tropicbirds, but native to temperate climates. They lived in the Miocene.
wikipedia.title: Heliadornis

wikipedia.extract: Amazon parrots are parrots in the genus Amazona. They are medium-sized, short-tailed parrots native to the Americas, with their range extending from South America to Mexico and the Caribbean.
wikipedia.title: Amazon parrot

wikipedia.extract: Hydrornis is a genus of pitta in the family Pittidae. The genus contains thirteen species, found in South-east Asia.
wikipedia.title: Hydrornis

wikipedia.extract: Sarcophanops is a genus of broadbills (family Eurylaimidae) found in the Philippines.
wikipedia.title: Sarcophanops

wikipedia.extract: Lithornis is a genus of extinct paleognathous birds. Although Lithornis was able to fly well, their closest relatives are the extant tinamous (which are poor flyers) and ratites (which are flightless birds).
wikipedia.title: Lithornis

wikipedia.extract: Pachylemur is an extinct, giant lemur most closely related to the ruffed lemurs of genus Varecia. Two species are known, Pachylemur insignis and Pachylemur jullyi, although there is some doubt as to whether or not they may actually be the same species.
wikipedia.title: Pachylemur

wikipedia.extract: The false potto (Pseudopotto martini) is a lorisoid primate of uncertain taxonomic status found in Africa. Anthropologist Jeffrey H. Schwartz named it in 1996 as the only species of the genus Pseudopotto on the basis of two specimens (consisting only of skeletal material) that had previously been identified as a potto (Perodicticus).
wikipedia.title: False potto

wikipedia.extract: Adapidae is a family of extinct primates that primarily radiated during the Eocene epoch. Adapid systematics and evolutionary relationships are controversial, but there is fairly good evidence from the postcranial skeleton (everything but the skull, or cranium) that adapids were stem strepsirrhines, members of the group including the living lemurs, lorises, and bushbabies.
wikipedia.title: Adapidae

wikipedia.extract: Djebelemur is an extinct genus of early strepsirrhine primate from the late early or early middle Eocene period from the Chambi locality in Tunisia. Although they probably lacked a toothcomb, a specialized dental structure found in living lemuriforms (lemurs and lorisoids), they are thought to be a related stem group.
wikipedia.title: Djebelemur

wikipedia.extract: Laccopithecus is an extinct monotypic genus of crouzeliine primate that lived in China during the Messinian stage of the Miocene epoch.
wikipedia.title: Laccopithecus

wikipedia.extract: Aegyptopithecus ("Egyptian ape", from Greek Αίγυπτος "Egypt" and πίθηκος "ape") is an early fossil catarrhine that predates the divergence between hominoids (apes) and cercopithecids (Old World monkeys). It is known from a single species, Aegyptopithecus zeuxis, which lived around 38-29.5 million years ago in the early part of the Oligocene epoch.
wikipedia.title: Aegyptopithecus

wikipedia.extract: Parapithecidae is an extinct family of primates which lived in the Eocene and Oligocene periods in Egypt. Eocene fossils from Myanmar are sometimes included in the family in addition.
wikipedia.title: Parapithecidae

wikipedia.extract: Nyanzapithecus is an extinct genus of primate from the Middle Miocene of Maboko Island, Nyanza Province, Kenya. This genus is known from four species.
wikipedia.title: Nyanzapithecus

wikipedia.extract: Notharctidae is an extinct family of adapiform primates found primarily in North America and Europe.
wikipedia.title: Notharctidae

wikipedia.extract: Notharctus is a genus of adapiform primate that lived in North America during the early to middle Eocene. Known from many geologic formations, including the Bridger Basin and the Devil's Graveyard Formation, Notharctus was wide-ranging throughout North America.
wikipedia.title: Notharctus

wikipedia.extract: Sivapithecus (lit. 'Shiva's Ape') (syn: Ramapithecus) is a genus of extinct apes. Fossil remains of animals now assigned to this genus, dated from 12.2 million years old in the Miocene, have been found since the 19th century in the Sivalik Hills of the Indian subcontinent as well as in Kutch.
wikipedia.title: Sivapithecus

wikipedia.extract: Brasilogyps is an extinct genus of New World vulture from the Late Oligocene or Early Miocene of the Tremembé Formation, Taubaté Basin, São Paulo state, Brazil. The type species is B. faustoi.
wikipedia.title: Brasilogyps

wikipedia.extract: Hadrogyps is an extinct genus of cathartid vulture from the Middle Miocene (Barstovian) Sharktooth Hill of California. It has been noted for its robust and collumnar tarsometatarsus.
wikipedia.title: Hadrogyps

wikipedia.extract: Paracathartes is a genus of extinct bird from the Wasachtian horizon of lower Eocene Wyoming. One species, Paracathartes howardae has been described.
wikipedia.title: Paracathartes

wikipedia.extract: The Pelagornithidae, commonly called pelagornithids, pseudodontorns, bony-toothed birds, false-toothed birds or pseudotooth birds, are a prehistoric family of large seabirds. Their fossil remains have been found all over the world in rocks dating between the Early Paleocene and the Pliocene-Pleistocene boundary.
wikipedia.title: Pelagornithidae

wikipedia.extract: Pelagornis is an extinct genus of prehistoric pseudotooth birds, a group of extinct seabirds. Species span from the Oligocene to the Early Pleistocene.
wikipedia.title: Pelagornis

wikipedia.extract: The Accipitriformes (; from Latin accipiter 'hawk' and formes 'having the form of') are an order of birds that includes most of the diurnal birds of prey, including hawks, eagles, vultures, kites, ospreys and secretary birds, but not falcons or seriemas. The generally nocturnal owls, also considered birds of prey, are a separate order from the accipitriformes.
wikipedia.title: Accipitriformes

wikipedia.extract: Gastornis is an extinct genus of large, flightless birds that lived from the middle Paleocene to the middle Eocene epochs of the Paleogene. Most known fossils have been recovered from Europe, although species historically assigned to the genus have also been reported from North America and Asia.
wikipedia.title: Gastornis

wikipedia.extract: The Actinomycetota (previously known as "Actinobacteria") are a diverse phylum of Gram-positive bacteria with high guanine-cytosine content (GC content or G+C content). They can be terrestrial or aquatic.
wikipedia.title: Actinomycetota

wikipedia.extract: Calidris is a genus of Arctic-breeding, strongly migratory wading birds in the family Scolopacidae. These birds form huge mixed flocks on coasts and estuaries in winter.
wikipedia.title: Calidris

wikipedia.extract: Zentrygon is a bird genus in the pigeon and dove family (Columbidae). Its members are called quail-doves and all live in the Neotropics.
wikipedia.title: Zentrygon

wikipedia.extract: Fowl are birds belonging to one of two biological orders, namely the gamefowl or landfowl (Galliformes) and the waterfowl (Anseriformes). Anatomical and molecular similarities suggest these two groups are close evolutionary relatives; together, they form the fowl clade which is scientifically known as Galloanserae or Galloanseres (initially termed Galloanseri) (Latin gallus ("rooster") + ānser ("goose")).
wikipedia.title: Fowl

commonNames.name: Grewcock's Sportive Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Lepilemur grewcockorum Louis Jr., Engberg, Lei, Geng, Sommer, Randriamampionona, Randriamanana, Zaonarivelo et al., 2006

wikipedia.extract: Grewcock's sportive lemur (Lepilemur grewcockorum), or the Anjiamangirana sportive lemur, is a sportive lemur endemic to Madagascar. It is a medium-sized sportive lemurs with a total length of about 55 to 63 cm (22 to 25 in), of which 26–30 cm (10–12 in) are tail.
wikipedia.title: Grewcock's sportive lemur

wikipedia.extract: Nannopterum is a genus of cormorant comprising three species. They are found throughout the Americas, hence the common name American cormorants.
wikipedia.title: Nannopterum

wikipedia.extract: Austral storm petrels, or southern storm petrels, are seabirds in the family Oceanitidae, part of the order Procellariiformes. These smallest of seabirds feed on planktonic crustaceans and small fish picked from the surface, typically while hovering.
wikipedia.title: Austral storm petrel

commonNames.name: Cruz Lima's saddle-back tamarin
commonNames.source: Catálogo Taxonômico da Fauna do Brasil

wikipedia.extract: Cruz Lima's saddle-back tamarin (Leontocebus cruzlimai) is a species of saddle-back tamarin, a type of small monkey from South America. Cruz Lima's saddle-back tamarin was formerly considered to be a subspecies of the brown-mantled tamarin, L. fuscicollis.
wikipedia.title: Cruz Lima's saddle-back tamarin

wikipedia.extract: The Colombian spider monkey (Ateles fusciceps rufiventris) is a subspecies of the black-headed spider monkey, a type of New World monkey, found in Colombia and Panama. The Colombian spider monkey lives in dry forests, humid forests and cloud forests, and can live up to 2,000 to 2,500 metres (6,600 to 8,200 ft) above sea level.
wikipedia.title: Colombian spider monkey

wikipedia.extract: The Azuero spider monkey (Ateles geoffroyi azuerensis) is a possible subspecies of spider monkey that is in critical danger of extinction according to the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species. Common names of this subspecies include mono charro, mono charao and mono araña.
wikipedia.title: Azuero spider monkey

wikipedia.extract: The large-headed capuchin (Sapajus apella macrocephalus) is a subspecies of the tufted capuchin monkey from South America. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru.
wikipedia.title: Large-headed capuchin

wikipedia.extract: Tropicoperdix is a genus of three species of birds in the pheasant family, Phasianidae. Although formerly classified in the now-defunct subfamily Perdicinae, phylogenetic evidence supports them being a sister group to the tribe Polyplectronini.
wikipedia.title: Tropicoperdix

wikipedia.extract: The Caquetá titi monkey (Plecturocebus caquetensis), also known as the red-bearded titi or the bushy-bearded titi, is a species of titi monkey endemic to Colombia found in the Department of Caquetá region. Taxonomically, it is a member of the "Callicebus cupreus group" (now Plecturocebus cupreus), following Shunsuke Kobayashi's Callicebus grouping.
wikipedia.title: Caquetá titi monkey

gbif.scientificName: Cheracebus Byrne, Rylands, Carneiro, Lynch Alfaro et al., 2016

wikipedia.extract: Cheracebus is one of three genera of titi monkeys. Monkeys in this genus, particularly the type species Cheracebus lugens, are sometimes referred to as widow titi monkeys.
wikipedia.title: Cheracebus

gbif.scientificName: Plecturocebus Byrne, Rylands, Carneiro, Lynch Alfaro et al., 2016

wikipedia.extract: Plecturocebus is one of three genera of titi monkeys. Historically, titi monkeys were considered monogeneric, being placed in a single genus: Callicebus Thomas, 1903.
wikipedia.title: Plecturocebus

commonNames.name: Milton’s Titi Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Milton's titi monkey (Plecturocebus miltoni) is a species of titi monkey, a type of New World monkey, from southern Amazon rainforest, Brazil. It was named after the Brazilian primatologist Milton Thiago de Mello.
wikipedia.title: Milton's titi monkey

wikipedia.extract: The Makassar tarsier (Tarsius fuscus), also known locally as Balao Cengke, is a species of tarsier. Its range is in Indonesia in the southwestern peninsula of the island of Sulawesi, South Sulawesi, near Makassar.
wikipedia.title: Makassar tarsier

wikipedia.extract: The collared nightjar (Gactornis enarratus) is a species of nightjar in the family Caprimulgidae. It is endemic to Madagascar.
wikipedia.title: Collared nightjar

wikipedia.extract: The common loon or great northern diver (Gavia immer) is a large member of the loon, or diver, family of birds. Breeding adults have a plumage that includes a broad black head and neck with a greenish, purplish, or bluish sheen, blackish or blackish-grey upperparts, and pure white underparts except some black on the undertail coverts and vent.
wikipedia.title: Common loon

wikipedia.extract: Allochrocebus is a primate genus including the terrestrial guenons: the L'Hoest's monkey, the Preuss's monkey, and the sun-tailed monkey.
wikipedia.title: Allochrocebus

commonNames.name: White-cheeked Macaque
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The white-cheeked macaque (Macaca leucogenys) is a species of macaque found only in Mêdog County in southeastern Tibet and Arunachal Pradesh in northeastern India. The white-cheeked macaque lives in forest habitats, from tropical forests to primary and secondary evergreen broad-leaved forests and mixed broadleaf-conifer forests.
wikipedia.title: White-cheeked macaque

commonNames.name: Bouvier’s Red Colobus
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Bouvier's red colobus (Piliocolobus bouvieri) is a species of colobus monkey rediscovered in the Republic of the Congo in 2015, after four decades without a confirmed sighting.
wikipedia.title: Bouvier's red colobus

commonNames.name: Lomami Red Colobus
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Lomami red colobus (Piliocolobus parmentieri) is a species of red colobus monkey from central Africa. Historically, it had been treated as a subspecies of the Central African red colobus (P. foai), but more recent taxonomies generally treat it as a separate species.
wikipedia.title: Lomami red colobus

wikipedia.extract: Miss Waldron's red colobus (Piliocolobus waldronae) is a species of the red colobus native to West Africa. It had previously been described as a subspecies of the western red colobus, P. badius.
wikipedia.title: Miss Waldron's red colobus

commonNames.name: Miller’s Grizzled Langur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Miller's langur (Presbytis canicrus), also known as Miller's grizzled langur or Kutai grey langur, is a species of leaf monkey. It is endemic to East Kalimantan on the island of Borneo in Indonesia.
wikipedia.title: Miller's langur

wikipedia.extract: The eastern black-handed tamarin (Saguinus ursulus) is a species of tamarin endemic to Brazil.
wikipedia.title: Eastern black-handed tamarin

commonNames.name: Ecuadorian White-fronted Capuchin
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Ecuadorian capuchin (Cebus aequatorialis), or Ecuadorian white-fronted capuchin is a species of gracile capuchin monkey of the family Cebidae. It was formerly classified as a subspecies of the white-fronted capuchin (C. albifrons).
wikipedia.title: Ecuadorian capuchin

commonNames.name: Venezuelan Brown Capuchin
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The brown weeper capuchin (Cebus brunneus) or Venezuelan brown capuchin is a species of gracile capuchin monkey endemic to Venezuela, although some sources also consider it to occur on Trinidad.
wikipedia.title: Brown weeper capuchin

commonNames.name: Panamanian White-throated Capuchin
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Panamanian white-faced capuchin (Cebus imitator), also known as the Panamanian white-headed capuchin or Central American white-faced capuchin, is a medium-sized New World monkey of the family Cebidae, subfamily Cebinae. Native to the forests of Central America, the white-faced capuchin is important to rainforest ecology for its role in dispersing seeds and pollen.
wikipedia.title: Panamanian white-faced capuchin

commonNames.name: Humboldt’s Squirrel Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Humboldt's squirrel monkey (Saimiri cassiquiarensis) is a species of squirrel monkey from Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela. It had previously been considered a subspecies of the common squirrel monkey, S. sciureus, but was elevated to full species status based on a genetic study by Carretero-Pinzón in 2009.
wikipedia.title: Humboldt's squirrel monkey

commonNames.name: Cazuza's Saki
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Cazuza's saki (Pithecia cazuzai) is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey. It is endemic to northwestern Brazil.
wikipedia.title: Cazuza's saki

commonNames.name: Golden-faced Saki
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The golden-faced saki (Pithecia chrysocephala) is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey. It is found in Brazil north of the Amazon, on both sides of the Rio Negro.
wikipedia.title: Golden-faced saki

commonNames.name: Hairy Saki
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The hairy saki (Pithecia hirsuta) is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey. It is found in northern Peru, southern Colombia, and a small portion of northwestern Brazil.
wikipedia.title: Hairy saki

commonNames.name: Burnished Saki
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The burnished saki (Pithecia inusta) is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey. It is found in central Peru and a small portion of adjacent Brazil.
wikipedia.title: Burnished saki

commonNames.name: Isabel's Saki
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Isabel's saki (Pithecia isabela) is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey. It is endemic to a small portion of northern Peru.
wikipedia.title: Isabel's saki

commonNames.name: Miller's Saki
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

commonNames.name: Miller's Saki | Red-bearded Saki | Monk Saki | Miller's saki

wikipedia.extract: Miller's saki (Pithecia milleri), also known as Miller's monk saki, is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey. Its range includes parts of southwestern Colombia, northeastern Ecuador, and perhaps adjacent areas in Peru.
wikipedia.title: Miller's saki

commonNames.name: Mittermeier's Tapajós Saki
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Mittermeier's Tapajós saki (Pithecia mittermeieri) is a disputed species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey. It is endemic to west-central Brazil.
wikipedia.title: Mittermeier's Tapajós saki

commonNames.name: Napo Saki
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Napo saki (Pithecia napensis), also known as the Napo monk saki, is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey. Its range includes parts of eastern Ecuador and northern Peru.
wikipedia.title: Napo saki

commonNames.name: Holland's Sportive Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Lepilemur hollandorum Ramaromilanto, Lei, Engberg, Johnson, Sitzmann & Louis Jr., 2009

wikipedia.extract: Holland's sportive lemur (Lepilemur hollandorum), or the Mananara-Nord sportive lemur, is a sportive lemur that is endemic to Madagascar. It is one of 26 species in the genus Lepilemur.
wikipedia.title: Holland's sportive lemur

commonNames.name: Makandé Squirrel Galago
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Sciurocheirus makandensis (Makandé squirrel galago) is a species of squirrel galago native to Gabon, Africa.
wikipedia.title: Sciurocheirus makandensis

commonNames.name: Bangka Slow Loris
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Bangka slow loris (Nycticebus bancanus) is a strepsirrhine primate and a species of slow loris that is native to southwestern Borneo and the island of Bangka. Originally considered a subspecies or synonym of the Bornean slow loris (N. menagensis), it was promoted to full species status in 2013 when a study of museum specimens and photographs identified distinct facial markings, which helped to differentiate it as a separate species.
wikipedia.title: Nycticebus bancanus

commonNames.name: Bornean Slow Loris
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Nycticebus borneanus, the Bornean slow loris, is a strepsirrhine primate and a species of slow loris that is native to central south Borneo in Indonesia. Formerly considered a subspecies or synonym of N. menagensis, it was promoted to full species status in 2013 when a study of museum specimens and photographs identified distinct facial markings, which helped to differentiate it as a separate species.
wikipedia.title: Nycticebus borneanus

commonNames.name: Kayan Slow Loris
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Kayan River slow loris (Nycticebus kayan) is a strepsirrhine primate and a species of slow loris that is native to the northern and central highland region of the island of Borneo. The species was originally thought to be a part of the Bornean slow loris (N. menagensis) population until 2013, when a study of museum specimens and photographs identified distinct facial markings, which helped to differentiate it.
wikipedia.title: Nycticebus kayan

wikipedia.extract: Miomancalla is an extinct genus of prehistoric flightless alcids that lived on the Pacific coast of today's California in the Miocene epoch. It contained two species, M. howardi and M. wetmorei.
wikipedia.title: Miomancalla

wikipedia.extract: Kuntur is an extinct monotypic genus of cathartid bird that lived in South America during the Tortonian stage of the Miocene epoch. Kuntur, the generic name, derives from the Quechua word for condor.
wikipedia.title: Kuntur

wikipedia.extract: Cariamiformes (or Cariamae) is an order of primarily flightless birds that has existed for over 50 million years. The group includes the family Cariamidae (seriemas) and the extinct families such as Phorusrhacidae, Bathornithidae, Idiornithidae, and Ameghinornithidae.
wikipedia.title: Cariamiformes

wikipedia.extract: The bare-legged owl (Margarobyas lawrencii), also called the Cuban bare-legged owl or Cuban screech owl, is a species of owl in the family Strigidae that is endemic to Cuba and Isla de la Juventud. It belongs to the monotypic genus Margarobyas.
wikipedia.title: Bare-legged owl

commonNames.name: Amazonian Black Howler Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Amazon black howler (Alouatta nigerrima) is a species of howler monkey, a type of New World monkey, endemic to the south-central Amazon in Brazil. Until 2001, most authorities included it as a subspecies (or simply a taxonomically insignificant variation) of the red-handed howler, though its distinction had already been pointed out much earlier.
wikipedia.title: Amazon black howler

wikipedia.extract: Phoeniconaias is a genus of birds in the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae. The genus contains one extant species, the lesser flamingo (Phoeniconaias minor), occurring in sub-Saharan Africa and western India, and an extinct species, Phoeniconaias proeses, from the Pliocene of Australia, which is thought to have been even smaller.
wikipedia.title: Phoeniconaias

commonNames.name: Groves’ Titi
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Plecturocebus grovesi Boubli, Byrne, Silva, Silva-Júnior, Costa Araujo, Bertuol, Gonçalves, Melo, Rylands et al., 2019

wikipedia.extract: The Alta Floresta titi monkey (Plecturocebus grovesi), also known as the Groves's titi monkey, is a species of titi monkey, a type of New World monkey, endemic to Brazil. It was described from the municipality of Alta Floresta in the state of Mato Grosso.
wikipedia.title: Alta Floresta titi monkey

commonNames.name: Ganzhorn's Mouse Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Microcebus ganzhorni Hotaling, Foley, Lawrence, Bocanegra, Blanco et al., 2016

wikipedia.extract: Ganzhorn's mouse lemur (Microcebus ganzhorni) is a species of lemur described in 2016. The discovery was made by researchers at the German Primate Center.
wikipedia.title: Ganzhorn's mouse lemur

commonNames.name: Kenya Coast Galago
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Kenya coast galago (Paragalago cocos) is a species of primate in the family Galagidae. It is found across Kenya and Tanzania, particularly around the northern coastal area of each of the countries, and has been located living from sea level to around 350 metres (1,150 ft) above sea level.
wikipedia.title: Kenya coast galago

wikipedia.extract: Ispidina is a genus of small insectivorous African river kingfishers. The genus was introduced by the German naturalist Johann Jakob Kaup in 1848 with the African pygmy kingfisher (Ispidina picta) as the type species.
wikipedia.title: Ispidina

wikipedia.extract: Sibirionetta is a genus of dabbling duck which contains two species, an extant species Baikal teal (Sibirionetta formosa) and the fossil species Sibirionetta formozovi from the early Pleistocene of Baikalian Siberia.
wikipedia.title: Sibirionetta

wikipedia.extract: The Anserinae are a subfamily in the waterfowl family Anatidae and includes the swan and geese. Under alternative systematical concepts (see e.g., Terres & NAS, 1991), it is split into two subfamilies.
wikipedia.title: Anserinae

commonNames.name: Heuglin’s Patas Monkey
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Blue Nile patas monkey (Erythrocebus poliophaeus) or Heuglin's patas monkey is a species of Old World monkey found in Africa along the Blue Nile river valley in Ethiopia, Sudan, and potentially South Sudan. While first described in 1862, it was synonymized with the common patas monkey (E. patas) in 1927.
wikipedia.title: Blue Nile patas monkey

commonNames.name: Robinson’s Banded Langur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: Robinson's banded langur (Presbytis robinsoni), also known as Robinson's banded surili, is a species of monkey in the family Cercopithecidae. It was formerly considered a subspecies of the Raffles' banded langur Presbytis femoralis, but genetic analysis revealed that it is no more related to Raffles' banded langur than it is to several other Presbytis species.
wikipedia.title: Robinson's banded langur

wikipedia.extract: Semnopithecus is a genus of Old World monkeys native to the Indian subcontinent, with all species with the exception of two being commonly known as gray langurs. Traditionally only the species Semnopithecus entellus was recognized, but since about 2001 additional species have been recognized.
wikipedia.title: Semnopithecus

commonNames.name: Eastern Pygmy Marmoset
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The eastern pygmy marmoset (Cebuella niveiventris) is a marmoset species, a very small New World monkey, found in the southwestern Amazon rainforest in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, and Peru. It was formerly regarded as conspecific with the similar western pygmy marmoset, but the eastern pygmy marmoset has whitish colored underparts.
wikipedia.title: Eastern pygmy marmoset

commonNames.name: Gursky’s Spectral Tarsier.
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Tarsius spectrumgurskyae Shekelle, Groves, Maryanto & Mittermeier, 2017

wikipedia.extract: Gursky's spectral tarsier (Tarsius spectrumgurskyae), also known locally as wusing, is a species of tarsier found in the island of Sulawesi in Indonesia. A recent taxonomic revision split this species off from the spectral tarsier and other tarsier species based on difference in vocalisations and pelage.
wikipedia.title: Gursky's spectral tarsier

commonNames.name: Jatna’s Tarsier
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Tarsius supriatnai Shekelle, Groves, Maryanto & Mittermeier, 2017

wikipedia.extract: The Jatna’s tarsier (Tarsius supriatnai), also known locally as Mimito, is a species of tarsier endemic to the northern Sulawesi, Gorontalo, Indonesia. Previously classified together with the Spectral tarsier, this species was reclassified and elevated as a separate species in 2017 due to their distinct and separate acoustic duet calls between males and females.
wikipedia.title: Jatna's tarsier

commonNames.name: Ankarana Dwarf Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Cheirogaleus shethi Frasier, Lei, McLain, Taylor, Bailey et al., 2016

wikipedia.extract: The Ankarana dwarf lemur or Sheth's dwarf lemur (Cheirogaleus shethi) is a species of dwarf lemur, part of the C. medius group, known only from northern Madagascar. It has been found in two reserves (Ankarana Special Reserve and Analamerana Special Reserve) as well as two protected areas (Andrafiamena-Andavakoera and Loky-Manambato).
wikipedia.title: Ankarana dwarf lemur

gbif.scientificName: Microcebus boraha Hotaling, Foley, Lawrence, Bocanegra, Blanco et al., 2016

wikipedia.extract: The Nosy Boraha mouse lemur (Microcebus boraha) is a species of mouse lemur described in 2016 from Madagascar. It was discovered by a team of researchers at the German Primate Center.
wikipedia.title: Nosy Boraha mouse lemur

commonNames.name: Bemanasy Mouse Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Microcebus manitatra Hotaling, Foley, Lawrence, Bocanegra, Blanco et al., 2016

wikipedia.extract: The Bemanasy mouse lemur, Microcebus manitatra, is a species of mouse lemur described in 2016 from Madagascar. It was discovered by a team of researchers at the German Primate Center.
wikipedia.title: Bemanasy mouse lemur

gbif.scientificName: Lepilemur grewcocki Louis Jr., Engberg, Lei, Geng, Sommer, Randriamampionona, Randriamanana, Zaonarivelo et al., 2006

wikipedia.extract: Grewcock's sportive lemur (Lepilemur grewcockorum), or the Anjiamangirana sportive lemur, is a sportive lemur endemic to Madagascar. It is a medium-sized sportive lemurs with a total length of about 55 to 63 cm (22 to 25 in), of which 26–30 cm (10–12 in) are tail.
wikipedia.title: Grewcock's sportive lemur

commonNames.name: Angola Dwarf Galago
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

gbif.scientificName: Galagoides kumbirensis Svensson, Bersacola, Mills, Munds, Nijman, Perkin et al., 2017

wikipedia.extract: The Angolan dwarf galago (Galagoides kumbirensis) is a species of dwarf galago native to Angola, and was named after western Angolan Kumbira Forest. Though 36 individuals of the Angolan dwarf galago were identified in September 2013, it was declared as a new species in 2017, and is now the nineteenth species of galago to be identified.
wikipedia.title: Angolan dwarf galago

gbif.scientificName: Wilaru Boles WE, Finch MA, Hofheins RH, Vickers-Rich P, Walters M & Rich TH., 2013

wikipedia.extract: Wilaru is an extinct genus of presbyornithid bird from Australia during the Late Oligocene to Early Miocene, around 26-22 million years ago. The type species is Wilaru tedfordi, and the second species is Wilaru prideauxi.
wikipedia.title: Wilaru

wikipedia.extract: Feducciavis is an extinct genus of sterninae that lived during the Middle Miocene.
wikipedia.title: Feducciavis

wikipedia.extract: Arenicolumba prattae is an extinct species of small pigeon from the Miocene of Florida. It was described from fossil material (a left coracoid) collected at the Thomas Farm Site in Gilchrist County, northern Florida, south-eastern United States.
wikipedia.title: Arenicolumba
